title: A semiconductor fab: sand to packaged chip, 400+ steps grouped
summary: Four hundred-plus fab steps collapsed into real process stages — from quartz sand to a packaged, tested chip — with awe kept proportional to the factories that earn it.

blocks.title: Four hundred steps that only make sense in stages
blocks.body: A modern logic fab does not feel like a recipe with 400 equal lines. It feels like a handful of giant stage machines — purify, grow, pattern, dope, interconnect, dice, package, test — each containing dozens of tool passes. This page groups the flood into those stages so a reader can hold the factory in their head.

items.label: Order of cycle time, wafer to packaged unit

blocks.heading: Stage map — sand to packaged chip

nodes.title: 1. Raw materials
nodes.detail: Quartz sand → metallurgical silicon → ultrapure polysilicon. Chemistry before any 'chip' exists.

nodes.title: 2. Crystal & wafer
nodes.detail: Czochralski (or float-zone) ingot growth, grind, slice, polish → prime wafers.

nodes.title: 3. Front-end device build
nodes.detail: Oxidation, deposition, lithography, etch, implant, anneal — repeated in loops to form transistors.

nodes.title: 4. Middle-of-line / contacts
nodes.detail: Contact openings, local interconnect beginnings — devices meet wiring.

nodes.title: 5. Back-end interconnect
nodes.detail: Multi-layer metal + dielectric stacks (damascene copper eras). Routing the city.

nodes.title: 6. Wafer finish & sort
nodes.detail: Passivation, probe/sort, ink or electronic binning.

nodes.title: 7. Singulation & assembly
nodes.detail: Dice, attach, wirebond or flip-chip, mold, balls/leads.

nodes.title: 8. Final test & pack
nodes.detail: Package test, burn-in where required, tape/reel or tray, ship.

blocks.caption: Already tens of steps before a lithography scanner ever fires.

blocks.heading: Stage 3: the loop that multiplies
blocks.body: Almost every transistor feature is a short refrain: clean → film → coat resist → expose → develop → etch or implant → strip → anneal/clean. Advanced nodes repeat that refrain across many layers and multiple patterning schemes. Counting each tool visit is how you reach hundreds of steps without inventing filler.

blocks.heading: One patterning loop (counts as many steps in the MES)
items: Deposit or grow a film (oxide, nitride, poly, metal hardmask…)
Expose (scanner / stepper); post-expose bake as required
Etch the film (or implant through the mask); strip resist
Clean; metrology; sometimes anneal or cure
Repeat for the next mask layer — dozens to hundreds of times

blocks.heading: Front-end building blocks inside the loops
Stages 4–5: contacts and interconnect stacks
rows: Every contact module is its own mini-flow
Dielectric, pattern, copper dual damascene, CMP, cap
Each metal layer ≈ a full patterning campaign
On some flows: extra RDL / stacking prep
Blurry line between fab and OSAT
blocks.caption: A 10–15 metal-layer part alone can dominate the step count.

blocks.heading: Stages 6–8: sort, assemble, test
rows: Ship only what meets the datasheet world

columns.name: Stage grouping (this page)
columns.detail: Eight stages, loops called out, metal layers acknowledged as multipliers. Same factory — holdable mental model.

blocks.quote: The awe is not the number four hundred. The awe is that each of those steps has a tool, a recipe, a control limit, and a person who notices when the limit blinks.

blocks.title: Node and foundry variance
blocks.body: Exact step counts, tool sets, and whether advanced packaging sits in-fab or at an OSAT vary wildly by node and company. This is a teaching map, not a proprietary process-of-record.
